investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM provisioning step at all.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of user-traffic or broader incident signals is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this eval.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 129s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=135961, confirming the check ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence keys were written, meaning the runner never advanced past pod scheduling to the VM-readiness or agent-creation steps.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at the scheduling layer before createAgent() could return.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 145s, no evidence keys — confirms the constraint persisted across the full eval window (~7.5 minutes from first to last check end).

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity simultaneously, the entire feature becomes unschedulable. A recent node label change or taint addition could have reduced the eligible pool.

Tertiary — VM resource quota set too low for the current workload level: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may be under-provisioned relative to demand, causing exhaustion under normal load.

Lower confidence — a leaked or stuck remote-agent VM from a prior eval run consuming a VM slot and not being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), though this would typically affect only one slot.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unused on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.
If re-running the eval immediately after the failure produced a passing result with all required evidence present, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.
If the pod spec for remote agents did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm at all, the scheduler message would implicate a different resource or affinity mismatch as the true cause.
If only one of the three sibling checks failed with the Unschedulable message and the others passed, it would suggest a transient single-slot exhaustion rather than full capacity depletion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but were excluded due to a recently changed node label or taint, the primary cause would be affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each eligible node before attempting remote agent creation, to surface exhaustion before the pod submission step.

Add a pre-flight eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes available), alerting early if the eligible pool shrinks.
Add a VM slot leak detection eval that periodically lists pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and flags any that have been running beyond the expected eval cleanup window.
Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes pod-scheduling latency from VM-readiness latency, so scheduling failures can be separated from VM boot failures in future diagnostics.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T23:33–23:38Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment was unable to schedule the kata peer-pod VM required to provision a remote agent. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were at capacity and preemption could not free any slots. The pod remained Unschedulable for 143 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no agent was ever created, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 (createAgent call) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster has only 2 nodes that carry this resource, and both were at capacity at the time of the eval run, leaving no room to schedule the probe pod. This is the most directly supported cause (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is always limited to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are saturated, the pod is immediately Unschedulable.

Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: other production or eval workloads may have claimed all available VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes before the eval pod was submitted, leaving zero capacity.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: preemption was explicitly reported as unhelpful and no new node was provisioned during the 143s window, suggesting autoscaling for this node pool is absent or slow.

Eval scheduling contention: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran in close succession (23:33–23:38Z), potentially competing for the same limited VM slots simultaneously.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM provisioning step at all.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of user-traffic or broader incident signals is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this eval.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 129s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=135961, confirming the check ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence keys were written, meaning the runner never advanced past pod scheduling to the VM-readiness or agent-creation steps.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting at the scheduling layer before createAgent() could return.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 143s, no evidence keys — confirms the same scheduling constraint blocked a second independent probe.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 145s, no evidence keys — confirms the constraint persisted across the full eval window (~7.5 minutes from first to last check end).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote', confirming the pod must be scheduled before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity simultaneously, the entire feature becomes unschedulable. A recent node label change or taint addition could have reduced the eligible pool.

Tertiary — VM resource quota set too low for the current workload level: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may be under-provisioned relative to demand, causing exhaustion under normal load.

Lower confidence — a leaked or stuck remote-agent VM from a prior eval run consuming a VM slot and not being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), though this would typically affect only one slot.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that periodically lists pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and flags any that have been running beyond the expected eval cleanup window.
Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes pod-scheduling latency from VM-readiness latency, so scheduling failures can be separated from VM boot failures in future diagnostics.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, so each pod timed out unscheduled and no agent VM was ever provisioned, leaving the eval with zero evidence collected against its contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints on the remote-agent pod spec. Because no node can satisfy both the resource requirement and the affinity/selector simultaneously, and because preemption found no evictable victims, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable indefinitely. This is a cluster-infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this infrastructure state; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots on the only 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, which may reflect intentional topology (only 2 nodes are provisioned for peer-pod VMs) or a configuration drift where nodes lost a required label or taint.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent demand from observability probes plus production workloads, requiring capacity expansion.

Lower confidence — stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from a prior eval run consuming VM slots without being cleaned up: if withCleanup (seen at run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) failed to release resources from a previous run, those pods could be holding VM slots.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. Identify which pods are holding VM slots and whether any are leaked or stuck from prior eval runs.

Check whether the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) successfully released resources from previous probe runs. If cleanup failed, manually delete any orphaned remote-agent pods to free VM slots.

If VM slots are genuinely exhausted by production workloads, evaluate whether the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes need additional VM slot capacity provisioned, or whether additional nodes of that type need to be added to the cluster.

Review the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec to confirm that the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded (topology design) versus having lost a required label or taint through configuration drift.

Re-run the full remote-agents eval suite after any remediation to confirm all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return passing status with complete evidence.

Note that this is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real cluster capacity constraint. Confirm whether production remote-agent provisioning requests from actual users are also failing before escalating to an incident.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the probe succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) with message containing 'hello from aura', the scheduling constraint has been resolved and this diagnosis no longer applies.

If kubectl describe on the pending pods shows a different failure reason (e.g., image pull error, resource quota, network policy) rather than Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, the root cause would need to be revised.

If the 2 nodes that carry kata.peerpods.io/vm show available (unallocated) VM slots when inspected, the scheduling failure would point instead to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
If the cluster has more than 6 nodes or the node count has changed since the eval ran, the capacity picture may differ from what the scheduler message describes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each eligible node and warns before slots are fully exhausted, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling fails.
Add a cluster-node-affinity eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules, catching label or taint drift before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a pod-cleanup verification step to the remote-agents eval suite that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each probe run, ensuring withCleanup is functioning correctly.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agent-create probe that validates VM slot availability before attempting full agent provisioning, allowing the eval to emit a more actionable 'insufficient capacity' status rather than timing out after 130+ seconds.
